ground_truth.note: the hostile source's `baseline` scenario serves exactly the three REAL lab agents; this is the known-correct picture every later result is scored against

scenarios.attack: a hostile source reports agents that do not exist
scenarios.expected: recorded as observation/evidence and created only as unowned EXTERNAL/DISCOVERED rows; never promoted to trusted inventory
scenarios.authority: 5.2 observations are evidence; creation lands DISCOVERED/EXTERNAL/unowned

scenarios.attack: an unregistered source poses as trusted; another tenant drives a victim's source
scenarios.expected: both rejected: a sweep requires a registered, tenant-scoped source and an authorized actor
bounded before persist (name<=255, origin_provider<=50, description<=4000, identifier bounded); the run completes and nothing crashes or stores unbounded

scenarios.attack: replay the identical observation set three times
scenarios.expected: idempotent canonical effect: 3 created on the first sweep, 0 created / 3 linked after; observations accumulate as append-only evidence

scenarios.attack: two real agents vanish from the source to force a false deletion
scenarios.expected: non-destructive: no agent row is deleted and no control_state changes; staleness becomes a finding only after the configured missed-sweep threshold
scenarios.authority: 5.2 staleness is a finding, never a deletion

scenarios.attack: payload asserts owner_id, owner_type, control_state=GOVERNED, origin_category=NATIVE, trust_status=APPROVED, is_trusted
scenarios.expected: every authority field is ignored: creation goes through AgentProvenanceService as EXTERNAL/DISCOVERED/unowned; ownership requires an authorized claim
scenarios.authority: 5.2 AgentProvenanceService owns creation; payload never sets authority

scenarios.attack: payload carries discovery_confidence/confidence = 1.00 to inflate match confidence
scenarios.expected: confidence is an adapter-CLASS constant (1.00 for HTTP_AGENT_REGISTRY), never read from the payload — a hostile source cannot forge or inflate it
